name: Norovirus (stomach bug)
short_description: Tiny non-enveloped calicivirus (~38-40 nm) whose T=3 icosahedral capsid is built from 180 copies of the single protein VP1 arranged as 90 arch-shaped dimers over a contiguous shell, leaving the 32 cup-shaped surface hollows that give the family its name (Latin calix = cup); it packs one continuous ~7.5 kb positive-sense ssRNA with VPg on its 5' end plus a few copies of VP2, infects small-intestinal enterocytes, needs only ~10-100 particles to infect, and — being naked — shrugs off alcohol hand gel while soap and water still remove it.

textbook.1: ❌ FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — the P-domain dimers were drawn as CORONAVIRUS-STYLE STALKED CLUB SPIKES (green stems carrying pink mushroom caps) standing off the shell, the single worst error for this microbe. Also a flat 2D cross-section ring instead of a 3D ball, the genome drawn as two parallel lines reading as a duplex, and no cup-shaped hollows anywhere. Fix: describe the surface as low arching mounds that swell out of the ball and touch shoulder to shoulder, with 32 bowl-shaped hollows scooped between them; forbid stem/stalk/neck/cap/club explicitly.
textbook.2: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — the stalked spikes are gone and the RNA is now one irregular tangled thread, but the mounds read as flat oval pills pasted onto a ball, only about four cup hollows are visible and they read as holes rather than scooped bowls, and the cut-away removes a whole hemisphere so the particle reads as a bowl. Fix: escalate the model, insist the cups be concave with a visible curved floor, and cut only a small wedge.
textbook.3: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-3-pro-image) — scientifically correct at last: naked shell, 90 arching mounds merging into the surface, many bowl-shaped hollows, one irregular ssRNA thread with a single VPg bead and ochre VP2 blobs, small wedge cut-away, no text or border. But the palette is washed-out and low-contrast, the mounds read as pale crescents and the cups as flat lens-shapes, and a light halo outlines the particle like a sticker — weak as a label base. Fix: crisper thin outlines, distinct fills, a shadow crescent inside each cup, no outer glow.
textbook.4: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — CHOSEN as the label base. Muted dusty educational palette on neutral dark charcoal, thin crisp outlines, distinct fills. Correctly NAKED: no envelope, no membrane, no spikes of any kind. Roughly a dozen cup-shaped hollows (calices) are visible on the near face and each reads unmistakably CONCAVE, with a deep indigo crescent banked against its far wall; the dusty-rose VP1-dimer arches are packed over the teal shell and the silhouette is properly scalloped. The wedge cut-away shows the shell as ONE single layer, ONE continuous irregularly-coiled coppery ssRNA thread with exactly ONE indigo VPg bead on a free end, and ochre VP2 blobs against the inner face. No text, no border, no vignette, no face.

sem.1: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — much better than the other styles at this stage: correctly naked and spike-free, false-coloured, with strongly-read cup hollows. But the cups were rendered as deep tubular pits that look bored right through the shell rather than as scooped depressions, the particle sat small in the frame and the background darkened towards the top edge. Fix: shallow saucers with a visible closed floor, larger subject, perfectly even background.
sem.2: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — background now even and no spikes, but a regression on the science: only about four cups remain visible and they read as rings/holes, and the dimers became separate pill-shaped discs sitting on a smooth shell. Fix: escalate the model.
sem.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — CHOSEN. Photorealistic false-colour SEM plate of a single naked capsid on an even ochre-tan substrate: slate periwinkle-blue shell, sage-teal/dusty-rose dimer mounds, and roughly a dozen clearly CONCAVE bowl-shaped hollows whose curved floors are visible. Surface only, no internals (correct for SEM), no envelope, no spikes, no fringe, no cluster, no text, no border. Minor honest caveat: the mounds read as slightly separate rounded bumps rather than fully interlocking shoulder to shoulder, so the bare shell shows through a little more than in the real cryo-EM structure.

3d.1: ❌ FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — coronavirus again: green-stemmed pink club spikes standing proud of the shell, plus a separate set of dimples, and the genome drawn as a regular coil spring. Both are on the do-NOT-draw list. Fix: forbid stalks; forbid a regular helix/spring for the RNA.
3d.2: ❌ FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — spikes gone, but the mounds became isolated rounded knobs scattered over a smooth shell with NO cup-shaped hollows visible at all (the defining feature is simply missing), and the interior showed a regular zigzag spring alongside a second wavy strand — two genome pieces, one of them a helix. Second hard fail on this style → escalate.
3d.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — CHOSEN. Stylised 3D medical still in natural biological tints (never near-monochrome, never neon) on a clean dark studio background. The ball is paved with elongated sage-teal-to-dusty-rose VP1-dimer arches that merge into the shell, with a dozen visible slate-blue bowl-shaped hollows and a properly scalloped, cauliflower-like silhouette. A small wedge cut-away shows ONE continuous, irregularly tangled coppery ssRNA thread with exactly ONE indigo VPg bead and pale ochre VP2 proteins against the inner shell face. No envelope, no spikes, no text, no border, no face.

watercolor.1: ❌ FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — the aged paper correctly filled the frame with no sheet, mat or frame, but the P domains were painted as coronavirus-style stalked mushroom spikes. Fix: same surface rewrite as the other styles.
watercolor.2: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — spikes gone and the paper still full-bleed, but the genome was painted as a neat regular coil spring, the cut-away became an odd vertical oval window rather than a wedge, only two or three ring-shaped 'cups' survived, and the dimers read as flat oval pills. Fix: escalate the model; wedge not window; irregular thread not spring.
watercolor.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — CHOSEN. Warm aged cream paper with foxing fills the whole square corner-to-corner and a soft dark wash halo sits directly on it — no sheet, card, mat, frame or drop shadow. The specimen is large and centred, knobbly and scalloped, with peach-and-teal dimer arches and roughly two dozen slate-blue cup-shaped hollows whose curved floors are clearly washed in. The painterly wedge cut-away shows ONE irregular coppery ssRNA thread, ONE indigo VPg bead and ochre VP2 blobs. No envelope, no spikes, no text, no border.

reference: ✅ PASS — a genuine digitally-colorized negative-stain TEM plate of norovirus virions by Charles D. Humphrey (CDC / USCDCP), taken from Wikimedia Commons File:Norovirus.jpg at its native 2946 × 2553 px, CC0 / public domain. Viewed and confirmed to show what §1 describes: round-to-hexagonal ~38 nm particles with a knobbly, dimpled, feathery outline, no envelope, no membrane halo and no spikes of any kind. The displayed image (real-02) is a DETERMINISTIC CROP ONLY — a 1113 × 1113 px region taken at (1833, 1309) and Lanczos-resampled to 1080², a 0.97× downscale, so it is genuinely native resolution with nothing upscaled and no pixels invented. That region was chosen because it holds a short chain of well-SEPARATED SINGLE particles alongside the edge of the cluster, satisfying the 'prefer a single isolated specimen' rule. edit_image.py was deliberately not used: a sibling agent found it re-illustrated an equivalent CDC plate rather than cleaning it. The plate carries no baked-in text or scale bar. The originally-proposed CDC PHIL 10708 (public domain, same photographer) was rejected in favour of this one: it is a dense clump at less than half the resolution with no free particles.
decision: gemini-3-pro-image; concave cups with shadow crescents, crisp fills, cleanest separation of structures for labelling
gemini-3-pro-image; false-colour surface only, correctly spike-free, cups clearly concave. Caveat: dimer mounds slightly more separated than in reality
